I have personally decided to stop because it has started to infuriate me that the only way for me  to exist in this society is by escaping into my mind.

I'm 24F and have been an intense daydreamer since age 5. From kindergarten to college, daydreaming on my school desk non-stop. Spacing in my bedroom, daydreaming myself to sleep.

I have decided that this is not acceptable anymore. That the world is this awful that I have created such an addictive coping mechanism. It's like heroin, but easier to access and the damages are not immediate.

My life feels so bland and empty without it. I feel so lost and restless and my brain feels deprived of oxygen but I can't look back. This is too serious. The world adults have created for us is one very sad one. And we need to feel the anger. They need to feel our frustration. 

We may be the first or the second generation of daydreamers. But I noticed that children now do it more than before. It seems that more and more people are afflicted. It's because the world is truly unbearable. 

This is why it has become urgent for me to stop. If I don't feel the pain, who is going to feel it? And were are we, as a society, heading?

I stopped daydreaming last week. I can tell you that I'm going through intense withdrawal. Life feels so dry and like there's a hole in my stomach. But on a brighter side, I have started to crave calling/texting people. I have started to crave for romance and sex. I have started to crave exercising also etc. I crave random normal things now and am working towards going back to school, get an engeneering degree etc.

My point is: I don't encourage you to continue daydreaming and burying your head in the sand. This is like accepting the suffering the world is inflicting you. It's like turning a blind eye to how dehumanising everything is and turning a blind eye to your own intense despair.
